concepts.title: Growth versus Development
concepts.definition: Growth is a quantitative, directional change (for example a rise in real income), while development is qualitative, value-positive growth implying improvement in human life; development is a process and both need not move together.
concepts.key_idea: Mahbub-ul-Haq and Amartya Sen reframed development as enlarging people's choices, not merely raising income.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy103.txt growth and development distinction and Haq-Sen references
question_patterns: differentiate growth from development with examples
why can growth occur without development
who pioneered the human development approach
what does development as enlarging choices mean
define value-positive growth
how is development both a process and a goal

solution_steps.explain: growth counts more output; development asks who benefits and how life improves
Mahbub-ul-Haq with Amartya Sen launched the Human Development Reports
enlarging choices in health, knowledge and resources defines development

concepts.title: Four Pillars of Human Development
concepts.section: The Four Pillars of Human Development
concepts.definition: Human development rests on four pillars: equity (equal access to opportunities), sustainability (continuity of opportunities for future generations), productivity (efficient use of resources, especially people) and empowerment (freedom and power to make choices).
concepts.key_idea: A development strategy missing any pillar fails: without equity the gains concentrate, without sustainability they expire.
question_patterns: name and explain the four pillars of human development
how does equity differ from empowerment
what does sustainability demand of present generations
why is productivity called a people-centred pillar
give an example where equity is violated
link empowerment with political freedom

solution_steps.explain: equity, sustainability, productivity and empowerment form the pillar set
inequity blocks access; unsustainability cancels future options

concepts.title: Approaches to Human Development
concepts.definition: Four approaches explain or measure human development: the income approach (linking levels to income), the welfare approach (state responsibility for welfare), the basic needs approach (minimum needs of food, education, health) and the capability approach of Amartya Sen (building people's capabilities to choose).
concepts.key_idea: The capability approach is the accepted core: development means expanding what people can be and do, not merely what they consume.
question_patterns: describe the four approaches to human development
what does the capability approach emphasise
how does the basic needs approach measure progress
criticise the income approach to development
which approach do Human Development Reports follow
relate welfare approach to state policy

solution_steps.explain: income, welfare, basic needs and capability are the chapter's approaches
Sen's capability approach underlies the human development index tradition
the shift is from means (income) to ends (chosen lives)

concepts.title: Measuring Human Development
concepts.definition: The Human Development Index combines three equally weighted sub-indices - health (life expectancy), education (schooling) and access to resources (income) - so the HDI can be estimated as the average of the three index scores, with countries grouped into very high, high, medium and low development classes.
concepts.key_idea: Averaging the health, education and income sub-indices gives the HDI value on a 0 to 1 scale.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy103.txt human development index dimensions and international comparisons
question_patterns: list the three dimensions of the Human Development Index
compute an HDI estimate from three sub-index scores
name the scholars behind the HDI

why is income converted to purchasing power parity
what does a low HDI value indicate

solution_steps.explain: health, education and income scores are summed
dividing by three yields the HDI estimate

solution_template.explain: income matters only through what it enables people to do
